title: Docs: add Grafana dashboard links + incident interpretation notes for scheduler class metrics
author: Julian Moore
commits: docs(runtime-metrics): add scheduler class dashboard UID + saved views
docs(runtime-metrics): add incident triage section for mixed workload tail spikes
chore(docs): fix broken anchor + normalize link formatting
ci(docs): update link-check allowlist for internal grafana host
body:
Summary: This PR updates the internal runtime metrics documentation to include direct links (Grafana UIDs + pre-filtered saved views) for the new scheduler per-class metrics dashboards introduced as part of the mixed-workload scheduler prototype. It also adds a short, incident-oriented interpretation guide so oncall can quickly distinguish “expected” queueing under mix from pathological head-of-line blocking, starvation, or token budget misconfiguration.

Context: During early canary + perf-canary runs, we repeatedly had to hunt for the right dashboard and re-remember which series mattered (queue time vs prefill time vs decode throughput). This PR centralizes the canonical links and provides a minimal triage flow keyed to the metrics we’re now emitting (per-class queue depth, time-in-queue, dispatch share, starvation counters, token budget overruns).

What changed (docs): Added a new “Scheduler class metrics (short/long)” section in docs/internal/runtime/runtime-metrics.md with the canonical dashboard link and UID. Canonical dashboard: Grafana “Scheduler: Class Metrics (Runtime)” UID: rw_sched_class_v2. Links include saved views with common filters: Hosted US-East (hosted-us-east-1), Dedicated canary pools (dedicated-us-east-canary), and per-model view (var_model).

Added interpretation notes (operational): Added a concise incident guide that answers: (1) If p95/TTFT regresses, is it queueing or execution? (2) Are short requests being delayed by long prefill? (3) Are we starving long requests under sustained short traffic? (4) Are token budgets causing artificial throttling? The guide explicitly points to: scheduler_queue_depth{class=short|long}, scheduler_time_in_queue_ms_bucket{class=*} (p50/p95), scheduler_dispatch_share{class=*}, scheduler_starvation_events_total{class=long}, scheduler_token_budget_overrun_total{class=*}, and prefill_latency_ms / decode_iteration_ms to separate “GPU slow” vs “scheduler slow”.

Added “If you see X, do Y” quick checks: - Symptom: p95 up, TTFT up, GPU utilization flat/low -> Check scheduler_time_in_queue_ms and queue_depth by class; likely dispatch skew or aging not kicking in. - Symptom: p95 up, TTFT stable -> Check decode_iteration_ms and token budget overruns; likely budget caps throttling decode iterations for short class. - Symptom: long completions stop progressing -> Check scheduler_starvation_events_total and time_in_queue for class=long; increase aging aggressiveness or reduce short burst cap (per runbook).

Cross-links: Added links from runtime metrics docs to the rollout runbook section “Mixed-workload scheduler: Monitoring checklist” and to SRE guardrails for tail latency canary rollback triggers.

Notes on link stability/security: These are internal-only Grafana URLs. For linkcheck CI, we allowlisted the internal Grafana host used by docs validation (previously causing a false negative). No public docs or customer-facing content touched.

Testing / Validation: Ran docs preview locally; verified links resolve and saved views load with variables. Buildkite docs linkcheck initially failed due to an anchor typo and missing allowlist entry; fixed and reran.

Rollout/Impact: No runtime code changes. Pure documentation + linkcheck tooling update.

Screenshots: (Not included) — dashboards are unchanged; this PR only adds canonical pointers and interpretation guidance.

Related: ENG-2441 (per-class metrics), ENG-2463 (SRE guardrails), SUP-19387 (hosted TTFT regression reports).
